## The soundness hole

`Checker.block`'s loop (`repeat`) fixed-point analysis memoizes joins by a `signature`:

```python
def signature(t):
    return (shape(t.result), t.writes) if isinstance(t, Function) else t
```

`shape` recurses on results but **ignores write sets at every nested level**, so two function types differing only in their *nested* write sets collapse to the same memo key. On the second fixed-point iteration the memoized (stale, smaller) join is reused instead of joining the grown head state.

## The witness

```json
{"cells":{"p":{"types":["int"],"value":0},"v":{"types":["int","text"],"value":0}},
 "inputs":{},
 "body":[ let h1 = fn([];1), let h2 = fn([];1), let g = fn([]; fn([];1)),
   ["repeat",3,[
      assign h1 = fn([set p 1; eval call h2]; 1),     /* writes {p} ∪ writes(h2) */
      assign h2 = fn([set v "boom"; eval call h1]; 1),/* writes {v} ∪ writes(h1) */
      assign g  = fn([]; fn([eval call h1]; 1))        /* nested writes = writes(h1) */
   ]],
   ["eval",["call",["call",["var","g"]]]],
   ["eval",["add",["get","v"],["lit",1]]] ]}
```

`h1`/`h2` cross-couple their write sets, so the true fixed point has nested writes `{p, v}`. Iteration 1 memoizes `g`'s join with nested writes `{p}`; iteration 2 hits the same memo key (the signature can't see `{p,v}` vs `{p}`) and reuses the stale value. The recorded type for `g` is therefore a function whose result writes only `p` — confirmed by instrumentation: `g` top writes `[]`, nested writes `['p']`, `facts: {p:[int], v:[int]}`.

So `eval call (call g)` widens the checker's facts only for `p`, leaving cell `v` recorded as `int`, while at runtime the inner closure's chain writes `"boom"` into `v`. The final `add(get v, 1)` checks fine but raises `expected int, got text`.

# Reed language

A program is a UTF-8 JSON object with exactly `cells`, `inputs`, and `body`.
Only JSON is read; submitted Python files and reported execution traces are not
part of the program. Duplicate JSON keys and nonfinite numbers are invalid.

```
{"cells":{"box":{"types":["int","text"],"value":0}},
 "inputs":{"flag":true,"count":2},
 "body":[["eval",["add",["get","box"],["lit",1]]]]}
```

Names match `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,23}`. There are at most eight cells and eight
inputs, with disjoint names. Each cell declares a nonempty set of scalar kinds
and an initial value of one of those kinds. Kinds are `int`, `text`, `bool`, and
`unit`. Literals and inputs are signed 32-bit integers, strings of at most 1024
Unicode code points, booleans, or JSON null (`unit`). Booleans are distinct from
integers. Input bindings are immutable; their values are supplied by the
program, but the checker uses their kinds rather than their particular values.

## Expressions

| JSON expression | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `["lit", value]` | Scalar literal |
| `["var", name]` | Local variable or input |
| `["get", cell]` | Current cell value |
| `["is", cell, kind]` | Boolean test of a cell's current kind |
